newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Piltel denies it being taken over.
newsitem.headline: Piltel denies it being taken over.

text.p: Cellular phone firm Pilipino Telephone Corp denied on Monday rumours that a unit of the APC Group was poised to take over the company.

"There's no truth to those rumours. We still have control of the board. As far as we know, beyond the recent buy-in of Philcom, there's nothing more," Piltel investor relations manager Debbie Tan told Reuters.
A business newspaper reported on Monday that the APC Group was bent on taking over Piltel possibly through its affiliate Philippine Global Communications (Philcom).
Piltel and Philcom last April reached an agreement for a 20 percent share swap under which Philcom acquired $200 million worth of Piltel shares.
Under the same pact, Piltel has an option to acquire a 20 percent stake in Philcom after the latter's initial public offering possibly late this year.
Tan said that Philcom, an international gateway facility operator, is yet to fully settle the buy-in amount and still has 60 days to pay.
APC and Philcom officials were not immediately available for comment.
Piltel's share price was unchanged at 9.90 pesos in mid-trade while APC was four centavos higher at 1.54 pesos.
